title: State-cache orchestration: tiered allocator and pipelined decode scheduler for paged attention
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Problem: Mixed-length workloads and multi-tenant bursts cause heavy fragmentation of the page-backed attention state (key-value 'state cache'), leading to suboptimal residency, frequent small evictions, and decode stalls when kernels must prefill scattered fragments. This ticket proposes a coordinated allocator and a pipelined decode scheduler to improve reuse, reduce tail latency, and provide predictable kernel-routing hints to the runtime.
background: Current behavior: the page allocator assigns first-fit page spans without tenant-aware soft reservations. When long-context traces intermingle with many short requests, we see fragmentation and increased page churn. The prefill stage (KV restore) for decodes can become serialized, exposing high p99 latency. Previous mitigation attempts (simple LRU tuning and larger stride thresholds) reduced churn for some workloads but regressed in multi-tenant scenarios. See incident notes and heap traces in incident/2026-01-kv-thrash.md.
proposal: 1) Tiered allocator: introduce three residency tiers (hot, warm, cold) with soft reservations per-tenant and per-model. Hot tier holds contiguous spans for low-latency reuse; warm tier accepts fragmented allocations with faster reclamation credits. Reservations are credit-based and decay on inactivity. 2) Fragment-aware compaction: background incremental compaction which consolidates small fragments into contiguous spans during idle cycles, guided by a compactability score. 3) Pipelined decode scheduler: decouple prefill/restore from kernel execution into a two-lane pipeline. Short decodes use fast-path without full prefill; long decodes warm the cache earlier and are scheduled into dedicated prefill slots. 4) Kernel hinting: expose occupancy and fragmentation metadata to kernel selection heuristics so kernels can prefer compact spans or use sparse-attention kernels when fragmentation is unavoidable. 5) Graceful rollout: feature-gated and opt-in by tenant, with observability to compare hit rates and tail latencies.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce p99 prefill-induced decode latency by >=40% for mixed short/long workloads on staging compared to baseline (staging-bench-2026-02).
Increase steady-state contiguous-span reuse rate (metric: contiguous_reuse_ratio) by >=25% for targeted tenants during 7-day canary.
No regression in overall throughput (qps) for single-tenant long-context workloads >95th percentile.
Documentation: design doc published and reviewed; runtime flags, config knobs, and metrics added to console dashboards.
E2E tests and load tests executed with pass/fail criteria automated in CI.
milestones: M2: Tiered allocator prototype + unit tests (2026-03-19)
M3: Pipelined decode scheduler prototype + integration tests (2026-04-02)
M4: Canary rollout to 5 tenants + monitoring (2026-04-16)
implementation_notes: Allocator will be implemented inside the paged-attention manager. Data structures: contiguous-span ledger, per-tenant credit bucket, hot-reservation ring. Compaction runs as low-priority background op bounded by GPU memory pressure signals. Prefill scheduler integrates with existing request router; implement greedy two-lane queue with backpressure to avoid head-of-line blocking. Kernel hints are lightweight metadata appended to runtime request descriptor.
test_plan: Unit tests for allocation / reclamation logic (race and stress).
Microbench: synthetic mix (80% short 20% long) to measure contiguous_reuse_ratio, eviction rate, and prefill duration.
Integration: end-to-end decode latency suite against staging runtime with canary tenant traffic.
Chaos: forced memory pressure tests to validate graceful compaction and backpressure behavior.
rollout_plan: Internal canary: enable for 3 internal tenants for 48 hours, verify metrics
Customer canary: opt-in for 5 low-risk tenants, monitor 7 days
Auto-fallback: if p99 latency regresses >15% for canary tenant, disable feature automatically and open rollback PR
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Background compaction could increase GPU memory churn. Mitigation: compaction runs with adaptive throttle tied to memory pressure and decode SLOs.
Risk: Credit-based reservations might starve bursty tenants. Mitigation: implement soft reservations with borrowable credits and preemption thresholds.
Risk: Kernel hinting may increase code complexity and cause selection bugs. Mitigation: keep hint paths additive (no semantic change) and add telemetry to detect misrouted kernels.
Risk: Edge cases with extremely fragmented cold pages. Mitigation: add emergency coalesce path that favors long decodes and uses streaming restores.
